title: LOV-LEDGER-EVENT carries 14 values in the TSD and 12 in the legacy story
source: RWB-E1-066 section 13 and section 8 BR1; TSD P3 v3 T5.1 (LOV-LEDGER-EVENT) and T-A.1 (interaction, DF-INT-014)
description: The legacy story loads LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with twelve values (CONTACT, LETTER, PROMISE, PAYMENT, HANDOVER, CASE_CREATED, CASE_ALLOCATED, CASE_TRANSFERRED, CASE_ESCALATED, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, DECISION_TAKEN, CORRECTION) and its section 13 calls that the whole list. The Technical Specification by Module for P3 prints fourteen values for the same list, adding PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER, and it is the higher source under R-PREC. This story neither invents nor drops a value: it reads the list as reference data of rwb-case, and the two values that only the TSD has are the ones the partner and offer channels need.
evidence: RWB-E1-066 section 13: 'list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with values CONTACT, LETTER, PROMISE, PAYMENT, HANDOVER, CASE_CREATED, CASE_ALLOCATED, CASE_TRANSFERRED, CASE_ESCALATED, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, DECISION_TAKEN, CORRECTION'. TSD P3 v3 T5.1: 'LOV-LEDGER-EVENT | CONTACT, LETTER, PROMISE, PAYMENT, HANDOVER, CASE_CREATED, CASE_ALLOCATED, CASE_TRANSFERRED, CASE_ESCALATED, DOCUMENT_ATTACHED, DECISION_TAKEN, CORRECTION, PARTNER_RESULT, OFFER'.
owner_role: rwb-case reference data owner and Compliance
proposed: Load the fourteen values of TSD P3 v3 T5.1 as the reference rows of LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, with PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER included and the Thai labels of DL10, and let RWB-P1-E1066-CON validate against the same list; the two extra values add no rule and remove none.

title: The ledger columns are required in the legacy migration and optional in the TSD
source: RWB-E1-066 section 13 (migration); TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 interaction DF-INT-014 to DF-INT-021
description: The legacy solution plan adds event_code, actor_type, actor_ref, source_ref, idempotency_key, case_seq, decision_log_id and corrects_entry_id as NOT NULL columns of the interaction table, apart from idempotency_key and the two references. The TSD prints every one of those eight columns as not required. The table is rwb-source-data's after the split, so the shape is fixed with RWB-P1-E1066-CON and RWB-P1-E1066-APP and not here; this story sends all five values its own rules require and reads back the sequence.
evidence: RWB-E1-066 section 13: 'adds to interaction the columns event_code varchar(40) not null, actor_type varchar(10) not null, actor_ref varchar(64) not null, source_ref varchar(60) not null, idempotency_key varchar(120), case_seq bigint not null, decision_log_id uuid, corrects_entry_id uuid'. TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 lists DF-INT-014 to DF-INT-021 with Required = No.
proposed: Keep the required flags of the legacy migration for the five values a ledger entry cannot do without, as the migration of RWB-P1-E1066-APP states them, and record the difference in the physical schema of rwb_source_data; this story is unaffected either way because it always sends them.

title: The case-side link table, its states, its key and the write order are not in the sources
source: RWB-E1-066 sections 4, 12 and 13; RWB-P1-E1066-CON (append and its four answers); TSD P3 v3 T-A.1
description: The monolith wrote the action and its entry in one transaction and needed no link. With the entry owned by another service, this story must hold one row that says which entry belongs to which case action, must fix the states of that row, must derive one idempotency key per action and must fix the order of the append and the local commit. None of those values is in any source read for this work package: the table name, its columns, the three state values, the key derivation and the reconciliation step are a target design choice, and the story states them so they can be reviewed once.
evidence: RWB-E1-066 section 4 steps 2 to 6 (one transaction, advisory lock, insert, commit) and section 12 (the Java interface with Propagation.MANDATORY); the append of RWB-P1-E1066-CON with 201, a replay, 409, 422 and 503 but no case-side state. No source names interaction_link, PENDING, COMMITTED or REFUSED.
proposed: Approve the link table interaction_link in rwb_case with the columns of 12.7, the three states, one key per action reference and the append-before-commit order; the sequence owner assigns the Flyway version.

title: API-P3-015 and API-P3-014 of the TSD have no rwb-case counterpart after the split
source: TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 API-P3-014 and API-P3-015; R-PREC default ruling (interaction ledger owned by rwb-source-data); RWB-P1-E1066-CON
description: The Technical Specification keeps GET and POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions as operations of P3 with the case record rights, and the legacy story uses POST as its endpoint. The Ownership Map and the default ruling give the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data, and RWB-P1-E1066-CON publishes the append and the case-filtered read on /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions. So the two TSD operations have no counterpart on the rwb-case base: this story provides no operation, consumes the append, and the case-side record path is the caller of that contract.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T-A.1: 'API-P3-014 GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions', 'API-P3-015 POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions'. RWB-P1-E1066-CON 12.1: 'POST /interactions' and 'GET /interactions' with caseId as a filter on the rwb-source-data base.
owner_role: rwb-source-data contract owner and the API specification owner
proposed: Retire API-P3-014 and API-P3-015 from the rwb-case API specification and keep the two ledger operations in the rwb-source-data document; the case-scoped read is the ledger read with caseId as its filter, and the recording screens call the append through the contract of RWB-P1-E1066-CON.
